summary: The README is wrong for the ankle; the data are dorsiflexion-positive and the prior audits' negation proposal is withdrawn. Seed 20261030 drew 6 subjects across both data phases (Phase1And2 BT10 decline 10, BT07 level 1.2 m/s off, BT11 decline 5; Phase3 BT02 level 2.0, BT24 incline 5, BT20 incline 5), 12 legs, 231 stances. (1) Foot frame from the publisher calcn-frame insole table (force norm equals the plate force to 6e-12 N): stance force up, CoP moves heel to toe in 231/231 stances, so +z rotation lifts the toes. (2) Lever-arm ankle moment (generic gait2392 talus offset): source ankle_angle_<side>_moment / dorsiflexion-positive internal estimate = 0.96-1.11 in 12/12 legs (correlation 0.987-0.999), same sign in 231/231 stance means, positive for every one of 9 ankle positions (0.77-1.49). (3) Level/uphill push-off net work positive in 154/154 stances (publisher power and own moment x d(angle)/dt identical); since sign(work) = moment sign x angle sign, the angle is dorsiflexion-positive too. Declines are not diagnostic (32/77 positive) and are excluded from that test. (4) Angle falls from 70 % stance to plate toe-off in 154/154 level/uphill stances; toe walking (measured CoP 12-17 cm further forward than heel walking) gives a lower ankle angle in 12/12 legs (BT02 L by 0.08 deg, BT11 R by 0.53 deg). (5) moment_filt_bio equals moment_filt for the ankle exactly and ankle power_exo is 0 (no ankle actuator). Exo encoder knee angle correlates +0.93 to +0.99 with OpenSim knee_angle and exo hip -0.90 to -0.99 with hip_flexion: the README hip/knee and exo statements are right; only its ankle statement is wrong. Moment/mass slope about 1 with README "w/ exo" masses is consistent with N*m/kg.

verdict.readme: wrong for the ankle (lines 90-91 "ankle plantarflexion is positive")
verdict.data: ankle angle, velocity and moment (net and bio) dorsiflexion-positive; moments internal (plantarflexor negative); not mislabeled relative to OpenSim gait2354
